purpose: Calcium is a mineral your body needs to keep your bones and teeth strong. It is also used to prevent or treat low calcium levels in your blood, and to help with conditions like osteoporosis. Some forms, like Tums, can also be used to relieve heartburn or upset stomach.
how_it_works: Your body uses calcium to build and maintain strong bones and teeth, and to help your heart, muscles, and nerves work properly. When you do not get enough calcium from food, a supplement helps make up the difference. It works by simply adding more calcium into your body so your levels stay in a healthy range.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are constipation, gas, and bloating. Some people may feel nauseous or have an upset stomach, especially if taken on an empty stomach. Taking it with food usually helps reduce stomach discomfort.
warnings: Do not take too much calcium, as very high doses over time can lead to kidney stones or other problems. Tell your doctor if you have kidney disease, as calcium supplements may not be safe for you. Calcium can interact with certain medications like thyroid pills, some antibiotics, and iron supplements, so try to take them at different times of day.
typical_dosing: Most adults need about 1,000 to 1,200 mg of calcium per day from food and supplements combined. Supplements are usually taken in doses of 500 mg or less at a time, since your body absorbs smaller amounts better. Take calcium carbonate (like Tums or Caltrate) with food, but calcium citrate (like Citracal) can be taken with or without food.
